Ashnah
ASH-nah
proper noun
The name of two cities in the lowland (Shephelah) of Judah, both named in the roll of Judah’s inheritance; the name is taken to mean “strong” or “a strong place.”

Biblical Definition

Ashnah is the name of two distinct cities in the lowland of Judah, the rolling foothills between the hill country and the Philistine plain. The first stands near the head of the lowland list: “And in the valley, Eshtaol, and Zoreah, and Ashnah” (Jos 15:33). The second appears further down the same catalogue: “And Jiphtah, and Ashnah, and Nezib” (Jos 15:43). That two towns bore the same name, both meaning strength or a strong place, tells of the character of the Shephelah — a borderland of walled towns and fortified holds, the shield of Judah against the Philistine. Yet the strength of these places was never in their walls. The Shephelah was ground fought over again and again, and Judah held it only as the LORD was her strength. “The LORD is my strength and my shield; my heart trusted in him, and I am helped” (Psa 28:7). The two Ashnahs preach, by their very name, the lesson Judah so often forgot and so dearly relearned: that a strong place is no defence when the LORD departs, and the weakest hold is safe when He is its wall of fire round about. The believer’s stronghold is not his own resolve or circumstance, but the name of the LORD, which is a strong tower into which the righteous runneth and is safe.

Webster 1828 Definition

The name of two cities in the lowland of Judah; the name means “strong,” fitting the fortified borderland of the Shephelah.

ASHNAH, the name of two cities in the lowland (Shephelah) of Judah.

The first is named near the head of the lowland list (Jos 15:33).

The second appears further down the same catalogue (Jos 15:43).

The name is taken to mean strong, or a strong place.

The Shephelah was Judah’s fortified shield against the Philistine plain.

Key Scripture

Jos 15:33 — "And in the valley, Eshtaol, and Zoreah, and Ashnah,"

Jos 15:43 — "And Jiphtah, and Ashnah, and Nezib,"

Psa 28:7 — "The LORD is my strength and my shield; my heart trusted in him, and I am helped: therefore my heart greatly rejoiceth; and with my song will I praise him."

Pro 18:10 — "The name of the LORD is a strong tower: the righteous runneth into it, and is safe."

Modern Corruption

A city of Scripture, not a contested doctrine; it recovers the truth that true strength is in the LORD, not in the walls and holds men trust.

expand to see more

Ashnah faces no postmodern redefinition. The truth its name carries answers the ancient folly of trusting in fortified places and human strength, as though a strong wall could stand when the LORD has withdrawn His help.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that the LORD is the strength of His people. Two towns named Strength guarded Judah’s border, yet Judah stood only as God was her wall; and the believer’s stronghold is the name of the LORD, a strong tower to the righteous.

Hebrew Roots

Two lowland towns of Judah bearing the name “strong,” guarding the Shephelah border, witnessing that strength is of the LORD.

expand to see more

Ashnah — the name of two cities in the lowland of Judah (Jos 15:33; 15:43).

The name is taken to mean strong, or a strong place.

Both stood in the Shephelah, Judah’s fortified border with Philistia.

Their strength lay not in walls but in the LORD who defended Judah.

The name of the LORD is the true strong tower of the righteous (Pro 18:10).

Usage

"Two towns named Strength guarded the lowland border of Judah."

"A strong place is no defence when the LORD withdraws His help."

"The name of the LORD is a strong tower into which the righteous runneth and is safe."
